summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration that defines two services: an app service built from the current directory that exposes port 8000, and a belgif-lint service that runs Maven to validate an OpenAPI specification file. The belgif-lint service uses a shell to run a Maven command while filtering out noisy warning messages from the output.

explanations.5: The double percent signs around 'port=8000' indicate this is a template variable that will be replaced with an actual port number at runtime, then mapped to port 80 inside the container.
explanations.7: This mounts the main.py file from your local machine into the running container at /code/main.py, so changes you make locally are immediately reflected in the container.
explanations.11: This specifies a pre-built Docker image (Maven with Java 17) instead of building from a Dockerfile, which is faster than building from scratch.
explanations.13: The ':ro' suffix means 'read-only', so the container can read your local files but cannot modify them.
explanations.14: This creates a named volume called maven-cache to store Maven's downloaded dependencies, so they persist between container runs and don't need to be re-downloaded each time.
explanations.17: By overriding the entrypoint to /bin/sh -c, we allow the command to use shell features like pipes (|) and redirection (2>&1) that wouldn't work with the default Maven entrypoint.
explanations.21: The '>' character allows the command to span multiple lines in YAML; all the lines below are concatenated into a single command string.
explanations.22: 'set +e' tells the shell to continue even if a command fails, so the container won't exit if Maven finds validation errors.
